summary.headline: Astrological Manuscript Fragments
summary.text: Description of a 14th-century paper manuscript formerly owned by A. Statius, comprising Latin and Greek fragments on solar and lunar eclipses, eclipse tables, circle and node measurements, exchanged nativities, and astrological inceptions. It cites Ptolemy’s Centiloquium, E. Martini, and parallel manuscripts, with excerpts on planetary terms, tropical signs, journeys, and lunar opposition to its own house.
